raw_case_text:
Patient is a 25-year-old woman from Guinea-Bissau, West Africa, and was admitted with an 18-month history of dorsal back pain, asthenia, and significant weight loss followed in the last 8 months by loss of the ability to walk.
On her physical examination she presented with three skin lesions (two ulcerated and one nodular) involving the right subclavicle region and other two lesions on her left thigh (one ulcerated and the other in a healing phase) (Figures 1 and 2); her neurological exams exhibited an ASIA A paraplegia with a sensory level at D4. Patient was anaemic with hemoglobin of 11,2 g/dL with an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 75 mm/h and a C-reactive protein of 5,26 mg/dL. Gamma globulin level was 44 g/dL and blood chemistry evaluation was normal. HIV and primary immunodeficiency testing were negative. A chest X-ray revealed an enlarged mediastinal shadow (Figure 3), and the spinal computed tomographic scan showed a large anterior and paravertebral abscess from D1 to D10 with significant compression and osteolytic lesions of vertebral bodies with a kyphotic deformity (Figure 4). Spinal magnetic resonance revealed significant compression of the spinal cord at the kyphotic apex and angulation of the column, anterior and paravertebral epidural abscess consistent with spondylodiscitis (Figure 5).
Bone biopsy revealed granulomatous inflammation with few acid-fast bacilli. Skin biopsy of the lesions (Figure 6) revealed acanthosis and pseudoepitheliomatous, hyperplasia of the epidermis, and necrosis foci surrounded by a histiocytic and lymphocyte infiltrate with giant cells on the dermis, consistent with tuberculosis with negative Ziehl-Neelsen stain. The patient was started on quadruple antituberculosis drug regimen together with pyridoxine and steroids, with a progressive clinical improvement, including healing of the skin lesions. One month later, anterior surgical debridement and posterior arthrodesis of the spine were performed. Blood and urine cultures including cultures for mycobacteria all proved negative. Cultures of the material collected through bone biopsy revealed M. tuberculosis. The patient fulfilled 15 months on antituberculosis medication and a favorable outcome was reported with complete recovery of neurological deficits.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 25-year-old woman from Guinea-Bissau presented with an 18-month history of dorsal back pain, asthenia, and significant weight loss, complicated over the preceding 8 months by complete paraplegia and multiple ulcerating skin lesions.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the 18 months prior to admission, the patient developed progressive thoracic back pain, asthenia, and marked weight loss, followed 8 months prior to admission by complete loss of ambulation and ulcerative/nodular skin lesions over the right infraclavicular area and left thigh.
subjective.past_medical_history: Native of Guinea-Bissau, West Africa; no known prior medical history.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for chronic thoracic back pain, asthenia, weight loss, paraplegia, and chronic ulcerating cutaneous nodules.

objective.physical_examination: Cutaneous examination revealed three right infraclavicular lesions (two ulcerated, one nodular) and two left thigh lesions (one ulcerated, one healing). Neurological examination demonstrated complete paraplegia (ASIA Impairment Scale grade A) with a T4 (D4) sensory level.
objective.routine_investigations: Blood tests showed anemia (hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL), elevated ESR (75 mm/h), elevated CRP (5.26 mg/dL), hypergammaglobulinemia (44 g/L), normal serum chemistry, and negative HIV and primary immunodeficiency workups. Blood and urine mycobacterial and bacterial cultures were negative. Chest X-ray showed a widened mediastinal shadow.
objective.advanced_workup: Thoracic spine CT and MRI demonstrated extensive osteolytic vertebral destruction from T1 to T10 (D1–D10) with severe kyphotic angulation, a large anterior paravertebral and epidural abscess, and severe spinal cord compression at the kyphotic apex. Vertebral bone biopsy showed granulomatous inflammation with scanty acid-fast bacilli and grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis on culture; skin biopsy showed epidermal acanthosis, pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, and dermal necrotizing granulomas with Langhans giant cells (Ziehl-Neelsen negative) consistent with cutaneous scrofuloderma/metastatic tuberculous abscess.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Extensive thoracic Pott disease (T1–T10 tuberculous spondylodiscitis and paravertebral/epidural abscess causing ASIA A paraplegia) with disseminated cutaneous tuberculosis (scrofuloderma/tuberculous gumma) in an HIV-negative, immunocompetent 25-year-old woman from Guinea-Bissau, confirmed by vertebral bone biopsy AFB microscopy and culture isolation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. She was treated with quadruple anti-tuberculosis therapy (completed for 15 months), pyridoxine, and systemic corticosteroids, followed 1 month later by anterior spinal surgical debridement and posterior spinal arthrodesis, achieving complete cutaneous healing and full recovery of neurological function and ambulation.
